conditions: Antibiotic exposure within 30 days prior to ICI initiation
findings: In RCC, associated with shorter PFS and higher primary progressive disease. In NSCLC, independently associated with shorter OS but not PFS after multivariate adjustment.
population: Advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)

conditions: Distinction between prior antibiotic exposure (pATB, ≤30 days before ICI) and concurrent use (cATB)
findings: Only pATB was associated with significantly worse OS and poorer response across multiple tumor types (including NSCLC and melanoma). Associations remained significant after adjustment for antibiotic class, performance status, and corticosteroid use in multivariate and propensity score analyses. cATB was not associated with impaired survival.
method: Prospective, multicenter cohort; routine clinical practice ICIs
population: 196 unselected patients with various solid tumors

conditions: Antibiotic exposure within 30 days prior to ICI initiation
findings: Associated with significantly shorter PFS and higher likelihood of primary resistance. Multivariate analysis confirmed antibiotic exposure as an independent predictor of shorter PFS. OS difference was not statistically significant.
limits: Sample size limitations for OS analysis.
population: Advanced melanoma treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-CTLA-4

conditions: Various definitions of antibiotic exposure around ICI initiation
findings: Consistently associated with inferior OS, PFS, reduced ORR, and increased PD. Strongest negative effects observed when antibiotics administered shortly before or after treatment initiation.
limits: Predominance of retrospective data; heterogeneity in exposure definitions; potential publication bias; precludes definitive causal inference.
method: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of retrospective cohorts
study: Tsikala-Vafea et al. (2021); Wu et al. (2021); Crespin et al. (2023)

conditions: Antibiotic exposure within 60 days prior to treatment initiation vs. after start
findings: Prior exposure independently associated with worse PFS and OS. Antibiotic use after immunotherapy start was not associated with impaired outcomes.
limits: Residual confounding inherent to retrospective analyses.
population: Treatment-naïve advanced melanoma receiving first-line anti-PD-1

conditions: Antibiotic exposure ±30 days or concurrent with ICIs/targeted therapies
findings: Antibiotic exposure associated with shorter PFS and OS across treatment modalities. Non-treatment-specific effect noted in Pinato (2023), highlighting vulnerability due to cirrhosis/infection risk. Alshammari (2024) found concurrent exposure associated with reduced OS.
limits: Complex clinical context of HCC (cirrhosis, gut-liver axis dysfunction); retrospective design precludes complete control of confounding.
population: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); Alshammari restricted to Child-Pugh class A/early B
study: Pinato et al. (2023); Alshammari et al. (2024)

conditions: Antibiotic exposure ≤3 months before or during ICI
findings: No significant impact on response rates or PFS (neutral finding).
limits: Limited sample size; highlights heterogeneity and context-dependence.
